title: Known unit phases preserve complete-cube posterior localization

localization.channel: On the complete cube, coefficients have known unit phases c_k and the normalized observation is c_k^* W_k=a_k exp(i(Theta+k dot Y))+xi_k with shell amplitudes and circular Gaussian noise bounded above and below.
localization.demodulation: Known phase multiplication is unitary and preserves circular Gaussian noise, so K1653's disjoint adjacent-pair and residual-subcube estimators apply without estimating c_k.
localization.risk: Translation risk is O(d_N^(-1)), global-phase risk is O(N^2/d_N)=O(N^(-1)), and normalized per-mode orbit prediction risk is O(N^(-1)).
localization.score_saturation: Posterior optimality gives M_(F,N)=O_(g,eta,R)(N^3) and R_(Omega,N)/4=C_(F,N)-O_(g,eta,R)(N^3).
localization.scope_guard: This requires complete-cube support, known unit phases, equal covariance magnitudes, fixed positive amplitude and a fixed four-parameter orbit; it does not recover unknown coefficients or growing latent dimension.
